newsitem.title: USA: Bonneville lowers firm, non-firm power prices.
newsitem.headline: Bonneville lowers firm, non-firm power prices.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration lowered its next-day for both firm and non-firm power delivered to the Northwest U.S. and the California border, the agency said Monday.
For Tuesday, BPA offered block power during heavy-load hours at $18.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) in the Northwest, down from $19.25 for Monday deliveries.
Deliveries of firm power at the California-Oregon border (COB) and Nevada-Oregon border (NOB) during the same Tuesday hours were offered at $19.50, down from $20.00.
Off-peak firm sales for all deliveries were offered at $15.00 per MWh, down from $15.50 for Monday pre-schedulings.
Non-firm offers were also decreased, to $20.00 for peak California border sales and to $18.50 for the Northwest, down from $21.50 and $19.50, respectively.
BPA offered non-firm power during light load hours for deliveries in the Northwest and California border at $15.00-16.00 for Tuesday, down from $15.50-16.00.
